prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map depicts a downward-sloping dirt trail where a person in a black jacket on the lower-left stands within arm's reach (roughly 0.4–0.8 m from the camera wearer), a person carrying a grey backpack stands ahead to the center-left at about 1.5–2.5 m (roughly 1–1.5 m beyond the nearest person), a third hiker in black pants stands further ahead and below at 2.5–3.5 m, and a fourth person in a cyan jacket descends wooden steps at the top-right around 4–5 m away. In frames 1–3, the hikers ahead face away down the slope and gradually retreat further down the trail while the nearest left person holds the camera wearer's hand at the bottom edge with upper bodies cropped out of view. In frames 4–5, as the camera turns leftward, the nearest person (wearing a pink mask) steps closer into the upper-left foreground (~0.3–0.5 m) and looks directly up toward the camera wearer while partially occluding another person standing just behind her left shoulder (~0.8 m away), shifting the backpacker to the right edge. Compared to the RGB strip, the depth map makes the continuous distance gradient along the uneven root-covered ground and the step-off to the wooden stairs much clearer at a glance. However, it is unreliable in frame 5 where heavy circular privacy blurs over the two close faces in the RGB image cause the depth estimator to hallucinate flat, overly bright white circular discs that distort true head geometry.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates up to four distinct people spaced roughly 1–2 m apart along the trail below the camera wearer: a close person on the left within arm's reach (~0.4–0.8 m), a hiker with a grey backpack and waist-tied jacket ahead (~1.5–2.5 m), a hiker in black trousers further down the slope (~2.5–3.5 m), and a distant hiker in cyan at the top-right stairs (~4–5 m). Across frames 1–3, the masks show the three distant hikers facing and moving away toward the upper-right while the close left person remains in the lower-left foreground with her head cropped out and her hand reaching the camera wearer's hand at the bottom frame boundary. In frames 4–5, the close person in the pink mask turns and looks directly at the camera wearer while filling the left foreground within arm's reach, and the backpacker shifts to the right side of the frame where the backpack is separately segmented in green in frame 5. The segmentation map cleanly separates overlapping dark clothing from the shadowed foliage and dirt background that blend together in the RGB view. However, the map is unreliable in tracking instance consistency (swapping mask colors across frames), completely misses the camera wearer's outstretched hand at the bottom of frames 2–3 and the distant cyan hiker in frame 1, and erroneously merges the masked foreground person and the occluded person behind her into a single pink 'person' mask in frame 5 due to the RGB face blur.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is almost entirely blank across all five frames, detecting only a single yellow body skeleton in the upper-right of frame 3 corresponding to the distant person in the cyan jacket descending the wooden stairs roughly 4–5 m in front of and below the camera wearer. That lone 2D skeleton shows the distant hiker's torso, head, arms, and one extended leg oriented away from the camera wearer and angled down the stairs to the right, with no other people within that person's immediate arm's reach. In this single detection, the skeleton makes the limb articulation and downward stepping posture of the partially occluded distant hiker easier to read than in the small, cluttered RGB region. However, the pose map is severely unreliable for overall scene understanding because steep egocentric viewing angles, heavy body truncation at the frame borders, and privacy face blurring cause it to completely miss the close person looking at the camera wearer (~0.3–0.8 m on the left), the person behind her in frames 4–5, the mid-ground backpacker (~1.5–2.5 m ahead), the hiker in black pants (~2.5–3.5 m ahead), and all hand skeletons including the held hands within arm's reach at the bottom of frames 1–3.
